Rest of tonight through Tuesday night: A deep area of low pressure 
located roughly at 140W 45N is directing a plume of Pacific moisture 
into the Northwest region. Widespread precipitation is push across 
the coastal areas Monday evening. We will see steady precipitation 
moving into the Cascades late tonight into Tuesday with a warm 
front. Light precipitation is expected to stretch as far east as the 
Columbia Basin and Okanogan Highlands; however, easterly flow into 
the Cascades with favorable orographics with the dynamics along the 
front will result in most of the precipitation occurring in the 
Cascades. Snow levels will be down to valley floors except along the 
Columbia River in the Wenatchee Area and along the Tonasket River in 
the Okanogan Valley where a rain/snow mix is expected. Stevens Pass 
is expected to pick up just a couple of inches. The NBM is giving a 
little more snow in the range of 2 to 5 inches at Leavenworth and 
Plain, and the Methow Valley, Loop Loop Pass is expected to pick up 
similar amounts. Snow will be heavier for travel over Washington 
Pass where 3 to 6 inches is expected through Tuesday morning, 
but then they'll pick up an additional 2 to 4 inches with the 
cold front passage Tuesday night. Expected winter travel, 
particularly along the North Cascades Highway and over 
Washington Pass. A Winter Weather Advisory remains in effect 
through Tuesday evening.

Wednesday through Thanksgiving: A weak to moderate Atmospheric River 
(AR) will be directed into the Northwest riding a 150+ kt jet streak 
at upper levels. P-wats increase to around an inch into the western 
portions of WA/OR and up to around 0.8 inches into the interior 
portions of the Northwest. The air mass will moderate with snow 
levels increasing. Precipitation increases over the region Wednesday 
night into the morning of Thanksgiving. Much of the Inland Northwest 
will wake up to valley rain, and snow will primarily be reserved for 
the higher elevations of the mountains (>5000 feet). The main 
concern for snow will be over Washington Pass where heavy wet snow 
may fall. The NBM indicates up to around 6-8 inches for the 75th 
percentile and 8-12 inches for the 25th percentile. Travel over this 
pass on Thanksgiving is not recommended. The cold front will 
push east of the Cascades in the afternoon when rain will shut 
off across the Columbia Basin, but looks to hang on across the 
Idaho Panhandle into the evening on Thanksgiving. All areas are 
expected to see at least a tenth to a quarter of an inch of 
precipitation. Favored upslope areas across the Idaho Panhandle 
will see totals in the range of 0.25-0.75 inches. The Cascade 
crest will pick up the heaviest amount of precipitation with 
between 1.5 to 2.5 inches expected. Slop over will bring 1 to 2 
inches of rain to Stehekin and the Little Giant Burn scar. In 
addition, the little bit of snow that has fallen over the 
Cascades will undergo some melting and the combination of heavy 
rain and snowmelt will result in rises along the Stehekin River.
We may also see runoff out of the Little Giant Burn scar where 
mud/debris flows will be a possibility.

Winds also pick up with the cold front passage on Thanksgiving. 
These winds don't look particularly strong though with south to 
southwest wind gusts of between 25-35 mph. A wet and breezy 
Thanksgiving. Not the best for enjoying a turkey trot in the 
morning. Wednesday and Thursday also will be the mildest 
temperatures of the week with highs in the 40s to low 50s.

Friday through Monday: There is more uncertainty in the forecast 
this far out in the extended period. Models show a quick hitting 
shortwave trough of lower pressure that pushes across for Friday, 
but model guidance shows varying degrees of strength this wave. 
Little confidence on the precipitation forecast because of the 
uncertainty. Temperatures cool a bit with snow levels a bit lower. 
Not cool enough for much of a risk of snow in the valleys though 
with precipitation over the weekend. Holiday travelers trying to 
make their way back home should keep an eye on the forecast though 
in case the forecast trends wetter that would bring a higher 
potential for snow over mountain passes. The forecast remains active 
into early next week as well. /SVH
